text:
Some motor carriers urge that the Chicago commercial zone be specifically defined rather than be determined by the population-mileage formula which they assert creates a zone which is also too broad. They point out that Chicago O'Hare Airport, which is a part of the city but not contiguous to it, would be used to expand the zone if the population-mileage formula is used. They argue that the population-mileage formula should not apply to airports which extend a city's corporate limits.
Motor carriers operating in the Los Angeles area object to the Interim Report's treatment of the Los Angeles commercial zone and the Los Angeles Harbor zone. They assert that the proposal restores the section 203(b)(8) exemption for traffic moving between the harbor zone and the commercial zone and renders the definition of the harbor zone merely a description for certain operating authorities. They contend that the main harbor area is separate from the main residential and business sections of Los Angeles and should continue to have its own zone.
Seattle area carriers object to expansion of the Seattle commercial zone to include the cities of Everett, Tacoma, and Bremerton, Wash. In support of their contention that these cities are not commercially a part of Seattle, they point out that they have their own city governments, courts and school facilities, operate their own ports, are served by different utility companies, and support industries which are unrelated to Seattle's principal industry which is aero-space. They also assert that the area west of Puget Sound which is included in the expanded zone is rural and residential in nature and is entirely separate from the city.
